title: MCH and MCHC (Red Blood Cell Indices)
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: MCH is the average amount of hemoglobin in a single red blood cell. MCHC is how concentrated the hemoglobin is within the cells.
low: A low MCH is associated with iron deficiency anemia. A low MCHC is associated with iron deficiency anemia or thalassemia.
high: A high MCH is associated with vitamin B deficiency anemia. A high MCHC is associated with hemolytic anemia or hereditary spherocytosis.
notes: The indices are read together with the other red cell measurements and the rest of the blood count, not on their own.
